title: Broadleaf stems: sampled step vs drawn heading
question: Which stand's branches read as grown wood rather than jitter?
context_md:
The complaint this is aimed at: **no plant has a smooth straight stem.**

The cause is not a weight that needs tuning. Eight neighbours cannot hold a direction — a shoot heading dead-on vertical scores straight-up at 1.0 and *both* upward diagonals at 0.71, so it steps off its own axis **59% of the time** however hard continuation is pushed, and because every step is an independent draw those departures pile up instead of cancelling.

So the sampled direction stops being the step and becomes a **vote on the heading**; the step actually taken is that heading drawn onto the grid the way a line-drawing routine draws a slope. Same weights, same weighted sample, same single dice roll per step — a shoot leaning 17 degrees still leans 17 degrees. Only the spelling in whole cells changed.

**What I already measured, so you can ignore it:** across four world seeds the same number of plants established either way (9, 8, 8, 8), and mean height moved +4%. Departure from a stem's own line, modelled on the trunk's own weights, falls from 0.88 cells to 0.41 (a perfectly drawn line is ~0.3).

**What I want your eye on:** whether the straighter one now reads as *drawn* rather than grown. That is the failure mode I am worried about and cannot judge for myself.
